extracted.intended_audience: public relations practitioners, PRSA members, communications professionals
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and standards from the Public Relations Society of America (PRSA) Board of Ethics and Professional Standards (BEPS) for ethical practice in public relations, including the PRSA Code of Ethics, case studies, Ethical Standards Advisories (ESAs), and heuristics for decision-making.

rubrics_metrics.name: PRSA Code of Ethics — core values
rubrics_metrics.description: The PRSA Code of Ethics sets out principles and guidelines that uphold the core values of the ethical practice of public relations, including advocacy, honesty, loyalty, professional development and objectivity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Code as the central statement of expected values and behaviors in PR practice; treat its principles as the foundation for decisions, client work, and professional conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize and acknowledge ethical issues
rubrics_metrics.description: As the public relations profession evolves, so does the need for revised and refreshed ethical standards. Ethical concerns and dilemmas occur daily; recognizing and acknowledging ethical issues as they arise is a primary responsibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain vigilance for ethical dilemmas in everyday practice; consult BEPS resources (case studies, ESAs, guides) when issues arise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use BEPS resources (case studies, advisories, handbook)
rubrics_metrics.description: BEPS provides an abundance of resources for public relations professionals — from case studies, Ethical Standard Advisories, ethics quiz, blogs and various resources including the BEPS Handbook.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult case studies and handbook materials (e.g., Eight Ethics Questions, Six Statements That Should Warn You) to inform decisions and to teach/guide others; use these as practical, educational tools rather than punitive instruments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical Standards Advisories (ESAs) are binding guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Applying the PRSA Code of Ethics, the PRSA Board of Ethics and Professional Standards (BEPS) offers analysis on current practice issues and challenges through Ethical Standards Advisories (ESAs). ESAs are considered direct extensions of the PRSA Code, and have the same force and effect as any provision within the PRSA Code.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat ESAs as authoritative guidance for novel or evolving practice issues; use them to interpret Code provisions and resolve practice questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure (ESA, 2018)
rubrics_metrics.description: An ESA addressing disclosure obligations (Disclosure, 2018).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the 2018 Disclosure advisory for expectations on when and how to disclose material relationships, sponsorship, or interests in communications and representations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics and Social Media (ESA, 2015)
rubrics_metrics.description: An ESA addressing ethical practice in social media (Ethics and Social Media, 2015).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply social-media-specific guidance on transparency, honesty, attribution, and responsible engagement when using social platforms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure and Transparency in Native Advertising and Sponsored Content (ESA, 2014)
rubrics_metrics.description: An ESA on disclosure and transparency in native advertising and sponsored content (September 2014).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure native/sponsored content is clearly disclosed and distinguishable from editorial content per the advisory's guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deceptive Online Practices and Misrepresentation (ESA, rev. 2012)
rubrics_metrics.description: An ESA addressing deceptive online practices and misrepresentation of organizations and individuals (Rev. June 2012).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid deceptive tactics online (fake personas, fabricated content, misrepresenting affiliations); follow the advisory when assessing digital conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Illegal Recordings (ESA, 2011)
rubrics_metrics.description: An ESA addressing the ethical issues around use of recordings that may be illegal (Illegal Recordings, March 2011).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not rely on or distribute illegally obtained recordings without careful legal/ethical assessment and disclosure; consult the advisory for acceptable practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical Use of Interns (ESA, 2011)
rubrics_metrics.description: An ESA about the ethical treatment and use of interns (Ethical Use of Interns, February 2011).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the advisory to ensure internships are educational, non-exploitative, and compliant with professional norms and labor standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plagiarism (ESA, 2010)
rubrics_metrics.description: An ESA addressing plagiarism and misuse of others' work (Plagiarism, September 2010).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid plagiarism; properly attribute sources and obtain permission where required; use the advisory for examples and corrective measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Looking the Other Way (ESA, 2010)
rubrics_metrics.description: An ESA and case study about ignoring or failing to act on unethical conduct (Looking the Other Way, August 2010).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not ignore unethical behavior; use the advisory/case study to identify responsibilities and appropriate responses when witnessing misconduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expropriation of Intellectual Property (ESA, 2010)
rubrics_metrics.description: An ESA on taking or using others' intellectual property without authorization (Expropriation of the Intellectual Property of Others, February 2010).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respect IP rights; obtain permissions and provide attribution as required; the advisory provides examples and boundaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Video News Releases (ESA, 2009)
rubrics_metrics.description: An ESA on the use of video news releases as a PR tool (Use of Video News Releases as a Public Relations Tool, October 2009).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure VNRs are not misleading, and disclose sponsor/creator relationships where relevant; follow the advisory for acceptable practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Questionable Environmental Claims / Greenwashing (ESA, 2009)
rubrics_metrics.description: An ESA addressing questionable environmental claims and endorsements (Greenwashing) (October 2009).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid making or promoting unsubstantiated environmental claims; ensure environmental assertions are truthful, supportable, and transparent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pay for Play (ESA, 2009)
rubrics_metrics.description: An ESA addressing pay-for-play arrangements and related disclosure issues (Pay for Play, October 2009).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose paid placement or compensation arrangements; avoid undisclosed pay-for-play that misleads audiences or media gatekeepers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representing Front Groups / Deceptive Practices (ESA, rev. 2008)
rubrics_metrics.description: An ESA on engaging in deceptive practices while representing front groups (Engaging in the Use of Deceptive Practices While Representing Front Groups, Rev. October 2008).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid representing organizations or campaigns in ways that conceal true sponsors or purposes; disclose affiliations and avoid deceptive representation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overstating Charges, Fees, or Compensation (ESA, rev. 2007)
rubrics_metrics.description: An ESA addressing overstating charges, fees and/or compensation (rev. August 2007).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Represent fees and compensation accurately; avoid exaggeration in proposals, contracts, and public statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure by Expert Commentators of Payments or Financial Interests (ESA, 2005)
rubrics_metrics.description: An ESA on disclosure by expert commentators and professional spokespeople of payments or financial interests (April 2005).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require experts/spokespersons to disclose relevant payments or financial interests that could influence commentary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Telling the Truth, Especially in War Time (ESA, 2005)
rubrics_metrics.description: An ESA emphasizing truth-telling, even in wartime contexts (Telling the Truth, Especially in War Time, January 2005).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize honesty and accuracy even under extreme circumstances; consult the advisory for ethical considerations in crisis/conflict reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting Unethical Behavior or Unprofessional Performance (ESA, 2004)
rubrics_metrics.description: An ESA (and resource) on reporting unethical behavior or unprofessional performance (Nov. 2004).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report concerns through appropriate channels (e.g., BEPS contact form); BEPS will attempt to respond and requests allow three weeks before re-contacting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of Employment Status of Client-Based PR Agency Staff (ESA, 2004)
rubrics_metrics.description: An ESA on disclosing employment status of client-based PR agency staff (May 2004).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be transparent about staff's employment and client relationships when communicating with media or stakeholders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Safeguarding Confidences (case study)
rubrics_metrics.description: Case study and discussion guide about safeguarding confidences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protect confidential client information; the case study provides scenarios and discussion points for appropriate handling of sensitive information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflicts of Interest (case study)
rubrics_metrics.description: Case study and discussion guide focusing on conflicts of interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify, disclose, and manage conflicts of interest; use the case study to explore practical steps for mitigation and disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competition (case study)
rubrics_metrics.description: Case study and discussion guide on competition-related ethical questions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engage in fair competition; avoid practices that undermine competitors through deception or unethical means.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enhancing the Profession (case study)
rubrics_metrics.description: Case study and discussion guide on actions that enhance the profession.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Act in ways that build public trust and raise the profession’s standards and reputation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical Decision Making Guide
rubrics_metrics.description: A guide intended to assist in ethical decision making (Ethics Case Study Ethical Decision Making Guide).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use structured decision-making steps and case-based guidance to resolve ethical dilemmas in practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Matrix of Ethical Dilemmas
rubrics_metrics.description: A tool (Matrix of Ethical Dilemmas) introduced to help identify and analyze ethical dilemmas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the matrix to map stakeholders, values, consequences and duties when evaluating difficult ethical choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content Issues — Free Flow of Information & Disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Case studies and discussion guides on content issues such as free flow of information, disclosure of information, and expropriating intellectual property.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support the free flow of accurate information; disclose material facts; respect IP rights and avoid misappropriation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Digital Issues — disclosure of deceptive online practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on digital-specific ethics, including disclosure of deceptive online practices and responsible online representation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply digital-specific standards (transparency, authenticity, disclosure) when operating in online environments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organizational Issues — representing front groups & use of interns
rubrics_metrics.description: Case studies and advisories covering organizational ethics topics such as representing front groups and ethical use of interns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure organizational-level transparency and fair labor/mentorship practices; avoid organizational deception.

rubrics_metrics.name: BEPS Handbook heuristics and checklists
rubrics_metrics.description: The BEPS Handbook includes items such as Eight Ethics Questions to Ask Yourself Before Acting, Six Statements That Should Warn You of a Potential Ethical Violation, Six Indications That Your Company Has an Ethical Culture, Eight Ethics Quotes, and Six Practical Recommendations for Building Employer Branding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these heuristics as quick-check tools for individual and organizational self-assessment and training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions of malpractice / unethical / improper behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: The page defines unethical/improper/malpractice behaviors as: a threat to the ethical practice of public relations; behaviors inappropriate or inconsistent with the Code; behaviors disruptive or that undermine ethical practices; practices and behaviors destructive to the reputation of practitioners, the profession or Society.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these definitions to identify conduct that violates professional expectations and to inform education and corrective guidance rather than punitive enforcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Education and inspiration over sanctioning/enforcement
rubrics_metrics.description: PRSA's modern approach emphasizes education, inspiration and motivating ethical behavior rather than sanctioning; the 2000 Code revision ended formal sanctioning because enforcement proved impractical for a voluntary organization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize educational remedies, illustrative examples of malpractice, and preventive resources; expect PRSA to provide guidance rather than adjudicative enforcement in most cases.
